stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and features new support via Ollama's MLX engine, including native DFlash and image input.

stories.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: The rapid expansion of data centers, driven by generative AI, poses a significant environmental threat.
The increased electricity demand from these new facilities risks reversing decades of air quality improvements in areas like Texas.
The reliance on gas-powered energy sources to meet this massive demand is highlighted as a primary driver of potential pollution.

stories.title: Meta to create a new class of shares to fund AI push
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta is creating a new class of non-voting shares to finance its aggressive AI initiatives.
The capital raised will also support potential acquisitions and employee compensation.
Trading for these new shares is scheduled to commence in 2027, reflecting the massive investment scale required for AI competition.

stories.title: Xbox wants you to pay 24 to 40 cents per hour to stream games you already bought
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Xbox is introducing a new monetization model where users pay hourly fees to stream games they have already purchased.
These time-based charges are an additional cost layered on top of the initial game purchase price.
This represents a significant shift in digital content consumption and ownership models within the gaming industry.

stories.title: RIP BioWare: EA shuts down storied RPG studio after over three decades
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: EA has shut down BioWare, a long-standing and storied RPG development studio.
The closure involves significant layoffs, reportedly affecting 400 employees.
A key consequence is the cancellation of the next planned project in the Mass Effect franchise.

stories.title: Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI Installs a Credential Stealer and Backdoor
stories.author: abhisek
bullet_points: A critical security vulnerability was found in the LiteLLM library (version 1.107.0) hosted on PyPI.
The compromise allows the installation of a credential stealer and backdoor.
This represents a significant supply chain attack risk within the AI/ML ecosystem.

stories.title: Eight Bits of Trust; eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds
stories.author: scotthelme.co.uk via pims
bullet_points: eMudhra's Certificate Authority (CA) keys were reportedly cracked.
The attack was described as being executed in milliseconds, indicating a high-speed compromise.
This represents a critical security failure impacting digital trust infrastructure.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and context gathering.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Tesla says customers can add their own vehicles to the robotaxi fleet next year — will it happen?
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Tesla has set a timeline for allowing customers to integrate their own vehicles into the robotaxi fleet.
The announcement came during Tesla's third-quarter earnings call, providing a concrete update on autonomous driving progress.
The feature relates to Elon Musk's long-standing promises regarding unsupervised autonomous driving capabilities.

stories.title: PHP: The three letters that shut down sites all over the internet today
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Critical vulnerabilities were discovered in the PHP programming language, a foundational technology for much of the internet.
The bugs are linked to AI components and have affected major platforms including 4chan, Wikipedia, and DeviantArt.
The issue is significant because PHP underpins numerous websites, including those built on WordPress.

stories.title: OpenAI's latest AI models are coming to Google Cloud and Antigravity
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: OpenAI's latest AI models (GPT 6.1 Astra, Sol, and Luna) are being integrated into Google Cloud.
This signals a deepening partnership and broader availability of OpenAI's advanced AI capabilities on major cloud infrastructure.
The news also mentions 'Antigravity,' suggesting a potential third-party or specialized deployment channel for these models.

stories.title: Report: Musk ordered Starlink slowdown in Ukraine, then blamed it on Trump
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: WSJ reports that Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of Starlink services in Ukraine.
Musk and Donald Trump have both publicly denied issuing such an order.
The story involves high-stakes geopolitical technology deployment and public denial.

stories.title: TenetBench: A Clause-Anchored Russian Corpus for Evaluating Language Models against Professional Codes of Ethics
stories.author: Sergey Bolovtsov
bullet_points: Introduces TenetBench, a new Russian-language corpus designed to test LLMs against professional codes of ethics.
Addresses a critical gap in AI evaluation: moving beyond broad harm categories to pinpoint specific ethical code violations.
Compares ethically challenging prompts against benign counterparts to isolate the impact of the ethical conflict on model behavior.

stories.title: Meta ordered to pay $25B penalty in New Mexico Cambridge Analytica case
stories.author: cbg0
bullet_points: Meta (Facebook) has been ordered to pay a massive $25 billion penalty.
The penalty stems from the Cambridge Analytica data scandal.
The action was secured by the New Mexico Department of Justice.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, Beam, available via Ollama.
Beam is specifically engineered for software engineering, reasoning, and complex agentic tasks.
The model is currently offered for free on Ollama Cloud for a limited promotional period.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local AI models within a cloud environment.
The integration allows AI agents to run safely on Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, deployable AI agent solutions.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama now integrates support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These decision models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers regarding yes/no questions, choices, or scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weights model ecosystems.

stories.title: Meta says it would’ve made over $22 billion if it didn’t have to pay a child safety settlement
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta disclosed in its Q3 earnings that a child safety settlement cost the company $9.89 billion.
The settlement payment significantly impacted Meta's reported income, which would have been $22.89 billion without the cost.
The financial penalty relates to a settlement reached with US attorneys general regarding child safety issues on the platform.

stories.title: Bose acquires Skullcandy to help it reach a wider audience
stories.author: Andrew Liszewski
bullet_points: Bose has acquired competitor Skullcandy in a strategic move.
The acquisition aims to expand Skullcandy's market reach.
Bose is integrating its advanced technologies, such as spatial audio and ANC, into Skullcandy products.

stories.title: Tesla profits drop 43% in Q3
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Tesla experienced a significant 43% drop in profits during the third quarter.
The company's energy storage division also saw a contraction in Q3 2026.
The news signals potential headwinds or shifts in Tesla's business performance.

stories.title: Does opting out of smart TV tracking work? Research finds “suspicious” traffic.
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Research suggests that opting out of smart TV tracking may not be fully effective.
The study found 'suspicious' network traffic originating from smart TVs.
The research author indicates that operating systems are unlikely to discard the collected user data.

stories.title: The Reflexivity Threshold: A Phase Transition for Multi-Agent Performative Prediction
stories.author: Roberto Di Pietro
bullet_points: The research addresses 'performative' learning systems where deployed predictions alter future training data.
It focuses on the complex stability issues arising in multi-agent systems where agents interact and influence each other's training.
The study identifies a specific 'spectral threshold' that determines whether multi-agent learning remains stable or enters a state of obstruction.

stories.title: Stochastic Pruning of the DPO Computation Graph: 1.4x Faster Training and Lower Peak Memory
stories.author: Tiewen Pan
bullet_points: Introduces a framework for stochastic pruning specifically targeting the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) computation graph.
The method achieves performance gains, reporting 1.4x faster training and reduced peak memory usage.
Pruning is achieved by independently sampling response positions, prefixes, and preference branches before computation.

stories.title: Block Diffusion for Longitudinal EHR: Accuracy, Efficiency, and Representation Trade-offs
stories.author: Alessandra Russo
bullet_points: The research proposes Block Diffusion (BD) as an alternative to Autoregressive (AR) models for predicting longitudinal Electronic Health Records (EHR).
BD addresses a limitation of AR models by handling temporally clustered and interdependent clinical events more effectively.
The study demonstrates a clear quality-efficiency trade-off when varying the block sizes of the BD model on the MIMIC-IV dataset.

stories.title: Mitigating Query Shortcuts in Chain-of-Thought with Context-Aware Decoding
stories.author: Shin'ya Yamaguchi
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting where LLMs may use query-specific shortcuts instead of relying on generated reasoning.
The paper investigates the efficacy of Context-Aware Decoding (CAD), a contrastive decoding method, to mitigate this shortcut behavior in CoT reasoning.
This work contributes to improving the robustness and reliability of LLM reasoning by ensuring answers depend on the generated rationale.

stories.title: Keeping Time vs. Understanding Time: Neither Alone Explains Temporal Reasoning in LLMs
stories.author: Nigel Collier
bullet_points: The paper challenges the long-held assumption that temporal reasoning in LLMs is strictly divided into 'temporal arithmetic' and 'temporal semantics'.
The authors present evidence suggesting that the traditional dichotomy used in benchmarking might be empirically flawed.
The research investigates whether tasks categorized as arithmetic or semantic in existing benchmarks actually support knowledge transfer.

stories.title: Rethinking Agentic Model Orchestration for Time Series Forecasting
stories.author: Ming Jin
bullet_points: The paper addresses the uneven performance of Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) in forecasting tasks.
It introduces FairAMO, a controlled evaluation protocol designed to disentangle whether performance gains from Agentic Model Orchestration (AMO) come from better selection or stronger models.
Experiments on GIFT-Eval confirm that AMO improves forecasting accuracy, even when controlling for candidate model strength.

stories.title: Parallel Thinking for Large Language Model with Path Diversity
stories.author: Ge Li
bullet_points: The paper proposes 'Parallel Thinking' as a method to improve LLM reasoning by exploring multiple paths concurrently.
A key limitation identified is that current RL-based parallel thinking suffers from 'mode collapse,' leading to redundant reasoning paths.
The research aims to address this homogeneity issue to fully realize the benefits of diverse reasoning trajectories in LLMs.

stories.title: A Strong MoE Is All You Need for Process Supervision
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: The research addresses the bottleneck of obtaining reliable process labels for multi-step reasoning supervision.
It proposes using the intrinsic expert routing statistics from Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models as a novel source of process supervision.
The study demonstrates that these routing statistics can provide an inherent process-confidence signal for training Process Reward Models (PRMs).

stories.title: Fragment-Level Graph Encoding for Interpretable Molecular Property Prediction
stories.author: Ina Pöhner
bullet_points: The research addresses the lack of actionable atom-level explanations in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) used for molecular property prediction.
The core innovation is changing the input representation by encoding molecules as fragment-level graphs derived from BRICS decomposition.
This fragment-level approach allows for more synthetically meaningful interpretations of GNN predictions without requiring a complete model overhaul.

stories.title: Unlocking Spatial Grounding in Flow-Matching Models via SNR Tuning
stories.author: Elke Hergenröther
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving fine-grained spatial control in image synthesis using flow-matching models.
It proposes that the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) distribution is a critical factor in enabling spatial grounding within these generative models.
The research suggests that existing Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have latent spatial representation capabilities that current generative models often fail to utilize effectively.

stories.title: The Reflexivity Threshold: A Phase Transition for Multi-Agent Performative Prediction
stories.author: Roberto Di Pietro
bullet_points: The paper addresses 'performative' learning systems where deployed predictions alter future training data.
It focuses on multi-agent settings, analyzing how interactions between learners affect system stability.
The research identifies a 'spectral threshold' that distinguishes stable learning from learning obstruction in these complex systems.

stories.title: Implicit Feature Reweighting for Label-Free Graph Generalization
stories.author: Lixian Zhong
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs).
Proposes SCARCE, a novel label-free representation-learning framework to handle distribution shifts.
Overcomes the limitation of existing methods that require class labels for determining predictive substructures.

stories.title: WRDO: Weighted Refusal Direction Optimization in Aligned Language Models
stories.author: Aleksandr Beznosikov
bullet_points: The paper addresses the fragility of refusal mechanisms in aligned Large Language Models (LLMs).
It suggests that refusal behavior is often mediated by a single, specific residual-stream direction.
The proposed method, WRDO, aims to improve upon standard constructions that aggregate heterogeneous harmful/harmless prompt information.

stories.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
stories.author: Alan Akbik
bullet_points: PACE introduces a new method for periodic and channel-aligned encoding of recurrent states in linear-attention language models.
The research addresses the memory and computational overhead of storing large recurrent states, especially when quantized to low precision (e.g., four bits).
PACE aims to improve the accuracy of four-bit state quantization, overcoming limitations reported by existing state quantizers.

stories.title: RCSD: Reinforcement and Continual Learning for Domain-Specific Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Lichen Pang
bullet_points: Introduces RCSD, a novel training framework for speculative decoding.
Addresses a limitation in current speculative decoding: reliance on soft-label distillation which degrades performance in high-entropy regions.
Uses Reinforcement and Continual Learning to improve the draft model's efficiency and acceptance rates during inference.

stories.title: pplx-embed-v2-late Technical Report
stories.author: Bo Wang
bullet_points: Introduction of pplx-embed-v2-late, a new pair of multilingual and multimodal models (0.6B and 9B).
The models achieve state-of-the-art results in text, image, and visual document retrieval benchmarks.
Performance highlights include the 0.6B model being competitive with much larger models on visual document retrieval.

stories.title: Beyond the Vote: When Do LLMs Add Value to Retrieval-Based Tabular Classification?
stories.author: Yingjie Li
bullet_points: Investigates the value of using Large Language Models (LLMs) for retrieval-based in-context learning (ICL) in tabular classification.
Compares four general-purpose LLMs against Distance-KNN voting using identical retrieved neighbors across 19 datasets.
Aims to determine if LLM inference provides a measurable improvement over simple voting mechanisms in this specific ML task.

stories.title: Mitigating Query Shortcuts in Chain-of-Thought with Context-Aware Decoding
stories.author: Shin'ya Yamaguchi
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting where LLMs may use query shortcuts instead of the generated reasoning.
The paper investigates using Context-Aware Decoding (CAD), a contrastive decoding method, to reduce this shortcut behavior in CoT reasoning.
This work contributes to improving the reliability and faithfulness of LLM reasoning processes.

stories.title: Keeping Time vs. Understanding Time: Neither Alone Explains Temporal Reasoning in LLMs
stories.author: Nigel Collier
bullet_points: The paper challenges the long-held assumption that temporal reasoning in LLMs separates cleanly into 'temporal arithmetic' and 'temporal semantics'.
The existing dichotomy influences how benchmarks are designed, models are trained, and progress is evaluated, but its empirical validity is untested.
The authors present evidence suggesting that tasks categorized as arithmetic or semantic in current benchmarks may not support expected transfer capabilities.

stories.title: A Strong MoE Is All You Need for Process Supervision
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: The research addresses the bottleneck of obtaining reliable process labels for multi-step reasoning using Process Reward Models (PRMs).
The core innovation is leveraging the intrinsic routing statistics of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models as a source of process supervision.
This approach provides an inherent 'process-confidence signal' derived directly from how the MoE model routes inputs to its experts.

stories.title: OmniSimulator: Aligning Small Language Models for Authentic Heterogeneous Behavior Modeling
stories.author: Hongyu Lin
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of current LLMs in accurately simulating complex, heterogeneous user behavior.
The proposed 'OmniSimulator' aims to improve user simulation by moving beyond shallow pattern matching inherent in native chain-of-thought.
The work focuses on aligning small language models to achieve more authentic and nuanced behavioral modeling for interactive systems.

stories.title: CVE-2026-107891: musl libc: multiple integer overflow in regcomp, possibly leading to incorrect allocation sizes and out-of-bounds heap writes
stories.author: openwall.com via dzwdz
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-107891) has been identified in musl libc.
The flaw involves multiple integer overflows within the regcomp function.
Exploitation could potentially lead to incorrect memory allocation and out-of-bounds heap writes.

stories.title: Multi-tier model routing on GKE: balancing Gemini 4 Argon reasoning depth with latency and cost
stories.author: olivi-eh
bullet_points: Focuses on building a high-throughput model routing gateway on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).
Addresses the practical challenge of balancing reasoning depth (Gemini 4 Argon) against latency and cost.
Involves dynamic routing between different model tiers (Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.8 Flash, local Gemma 4).

stories.title: Idempotency keys for AI agents: why hashing the arguments doesn't work
stories.author: anis_meziani_52aab42304a8
bullet_points: The article addresses a critical issue in AI agent design: ensuring idempotency during run replays.
Hashing generated content (like rewritten emails) is unreliable for idempotency because the content changes upon replay.
The solution proposed is that idempotency keys must be derived from the stable intent of the agent, not the volatile output.
